name: 18922-visionchat-4b-1gpu
model: unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it -- the ungated mirror of google/gemma-3-4b-it, same weights. The Gemma Terms of Use apply.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine. A 4B model fits one card.
architecture: Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration, bf16, 8.6 GB of safetensors: 34-layer text tower, siglip_vision_model tower of 27 layers (hidden 1152, image_size 896, patch_size 14), mm_tokens_per_image 256.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 10% (= 400 requests, so 3600 of the 4000 are scored), no cooldown phase, bounded at 4000 requests with a 900 s safety cap. The engine runs at the batch budget the report's own card was in -- max-num-batched-tokens 2048 / max-num-seqs 256. `mm-processor-kwargs: {use_fast: true}` is set as well: `AsyncLLM.add_request` runs `process_inputs` synchronously on the frontend event loop, so its per-request CPU cost is an admission ceiling for the whole run, and the checkpoint's saved slow processor costs 38.5 CPU ms/request (~26 req/s) against the fast one's 22.5. Prompt shapes are byte-identical either way.
workload: single-turn image chat: one image plus a short text prompt per request, 117 output tokens. Shape: 97 prompt tokens, 117 output tokens, 4000 requests -- the report's per-request shape, with the request count raised from its own 985 completions because those took 89 s on an L40S and would be a far shorter scored window on hardware ~4x faster; its client was in fact asked for 5000 prompts. Prompts and images are synthetic and distinct per request; image geometry is 1024x768 JPEG, which the processor resizes to 896x896. Image CONTENT is `solid` (a per-row random RGB), not the deserializer's default `gradient`: the client synthesizes every image inline on one producer thread, and gradient costs 65 CPU ms/image against solid's 6.6, which on its own would cap the client at ~15 req/s. Content changes nothing the engine does -- same 896x896 resize, same 256 image tokens -- and 400 of 400 sampled rows are byte-distinct, so the multimodal cache is defeated exactly as it was before. On the wire the engine sees 360 tokens per request, of which a 260-token image region at offset 1 -- that engine count, not the declared 97, is what the client reports.
purpose: A single-image visual chat assistant giving short answers to 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# A plain `vllm serve` of this checkpoint on one H100, with nothing tuned.

model: unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# The batch budget the REPORT'S CARD self-configured to, not this card's. `_set_default_args_v1`
# keys off device memory: a < 70 GiB card (the report's L40S, 48 GB) gets 2048 / 256, an >= 70 GiB
# non-A100 card gets 8192 / 1024. The report ran a plain `vllm serve` with no batch flags, so
# 2048 / 256 is what its engine actually ran at; writing the H100 branch's 8192 / 1024 here would
# reproduce the report's command line while putting the scheduler in a batch regime the report
# never measured. Written out explicitly; it applies to every run.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
max-num-seqs: 256

# The engine's own defaults at this commit, written out so they cannot drift.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: true

# A request is under 500 tokens; the checkpoint's own window is 131072.
max-model-len: 8192

# CLIENT-SIDE CEILING REMOVAL, not a tuning knob. `AsyncLLM.add_request` calls
# `processor.process_inputs` synchronously on the frontend event loop, so its per-request CPU cost
# is a hard admission ceiling for the whole run. Measured single-threaded on this cluster's Xeon
# 8481C: 38.5 CPU ms/request with the checkpoint's saved slow (PIL) image processor = ~26 req/s,
# against a card expected to serve appreciably more than that. `use_fast` selects the torchvision
# implementation -- 22.5 CPU ms/request single-threaded, and it threads on a real node -- so the
# GPU rather than one Python thread decides the result. Verified to emit byte-identical prompt
# shapes (354 tokens, 256 image tokens) either way; only the resample kernel differs.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"use_fast": true}
